title: Repeated Subtrees in a Tree
statement:
You get the root of a binary tree. A subtree is a node together with all of its descendants. Two subtrees are equal when they have the same shape and the same value at every matching position.

Find every subtree that occurs at least twice. Return one copy of each, as a list of tree roots in any order. Each copy is shown as its level-order array, and the outer list order does not matter.

examples.why: The node 2 with a left child 4 appears twice (under 1 and under 3). The leaf 4 appears three times, but is listed once.
The two leaves are equal. The root is unique: no other subtree has three nodes.
Both 2-nodes have one child 3, but on different sides. Mirror images are not equal, so only the leaf 3 repeats.

hints: How could you turn a whole subtree into one value that you can put in a hash map?
Serialize each subtree bottom-up, for example as "left,val,right" with a marker for empty children. Equal subtrees give equal strings, and the markers keep different shapes apart.
Count the serializations in a map and add a node to the answer exactly when its count reaches 2. To avoid long strings, give each distinct (leftId, val, rightId) triple a small integer id instead.

explain.intuition:
Comparing subtrees pair by pair is slow. Instead, give every subtree a fingerprint that is equal exactly when the subtrees are equal, and count fingerprints in a hash map, the same way you would dedupe JSON objects by their stringified form.

A post-order walk builds the fingerprints bottom-up: a node's fingerprint is made from its left child's, its value and its right child's, with a marker for a missing child so that a left-only child and a right-only child differ. Strings work but can be long. Assigning each distinct triple (leftId, val, rightId) a fresh integer id keeps every fingerprint O(1) in size.
steps: Walk the tree in post-order, so both children get their ids first. An empty child has id 0.
Make the key leftId,val,rightId. If the key is new, give it the next integer id.
Increase the count of that id. When the count becomes exactly 2, add the current node to the answer.
pitfalls: Serializing without null markers. Then 2 → left 3 and 2 → right 3 give the same string.
Adding a node every time its count is ≥ 2. A subtree seen three times would be reported twice.
Using in-order serialization. It cannot tell some different shapes apart, even with markers placed carelessly.

solutions.title: Compare every pair of subtrees
solutions.idea: Collect all nodes. For each node, check whether an earlier node has an equal subtree and whether this shape was already reported.

solutions.title: Serialize every subtree to a string
solutions.idea: Post-order build "(left)val(right)" strings with a marker for empty children; report a node when its string is seen the second time.
solutions.time: O(n²) in the worst case (string length)

solutions.title: Integer id per (left, value, right) triple
solutions.idea: Same post-order walk, but each distinct triple of child ids and value gets a small integer id, so every key has constant size.

followups: Treat a subtree and its mirror image as equal. How do you change the fingerprint?
The tree is deep enough to overflow the call stack. How do you do the post-order walk iteratively?
